subject.title: [Bug]: Unscheduled reminder guard fires for isolated-session crons + counter lost during compaction

question: Should maintainers adopt or refresh the open full-fix fork PR, land the same-repo partial compaction PR first, or open a target-repo replacement covering both reported gaps?
rationale: The bug is source-proven, but there are overlapping open fix paths with different scope and mergeability, so automation should not create another duplicate repair branch before maintainers choose ownership and scope.

options.title: Adopt Or Replace Full Fix
options.body: Use the fork PR as source material or open a narrow target-repo replacement that covers both isolated-cron matching and compaction-counter preservation with regression tests.

options.title: Land Partial Compaction Fix First
options.body: Proceed with the same-repo compaction PR while keeping this issue open for the isolated-session cron gap.

options.title: Wait On Fork Refresh
options.body: Keep this issue paired with the fork PR and wait for the contributor to resolve conflicts, proof, and current-main drift.

recommendation.title: Adopt Or Replace Full Fix
recommendation.body: Use the fork PR as source material or open a narrow target-repo replacement that covers both isolated-cron matching and compaction-counter preservation with regression tests.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the most relevant available routing owner from prior merge/refactor history on the reminder guard and embedded-agent surfaces.
